## Purpose and System Boundary

This page shows how the electrical-infrastructure pages fit together and where each assumption is maintained. It does not introduce separate component assumptions.

The electrical chain begins after the turbine inverter and before the turbine step-up transformer. For electricity export, it ends at the onshore grid connection point. The reference architecture uses 66 kV AC array collection and a 525 kV HVDC export system based on TenneT's 2 GW standard [@tennet2024TwoGWProgram; @tennet2025TwoGWStandard].

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-height: 0.5
flowchart LR
  A["Turbine inverter"] --> B["Turbine transformer"]
  B --> C["66 kV array network"]
  C --> D["Offshore AC collection"]
  D --> E["Offshore VSC converter"]
  E --> F["±525 kV HVDC cable system"]
  F --> G["Onshore VSC converter"]
  G --> H["Onshore grid interface"]
```

## Architecture Applicability

| Component | Electricity export | Centralised hydrogen | Decentralised hydrogen |
|---|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| Turbine step-up transformer | Used | Used | Removed from the main conversion path |
| 66 kV array network | Used | Used | Replaced by hydrogen collection |
| Offshore AC aggregation | Used | Used, without HVDC export equipment | No central station |
| Offshore and onshore HVDC converters | Used | Not used | Not used |
| HVDC export-cable system | Used | Not used | Not used |
| Onshore electrical grid connection | Used | Not used | Not used |

The centralised-hydrogen architecture diverges from electricity export at the offshore collection point. Its transformer and rectifier assumptions are maintained on [Electrolyser Power Electronics](../hydrogen_production/elx_power_electronics.qmd).

::: {.callout-important}
## Book each cost and performance effect once

Component pages may repeat linked values to put their own scope in perspective. The owner columns determine where a value is booked. Grey cost labels are references to another page; green labels identify costs owned by the page on which they appear.

The same rule applies to performance: a detailed loss or outage calculation replaces the corresponding flat efficiency or availability factor rather than being added to it.
:::
